name: SIIM-ISIC Melanoma Classification 1st Place — Multi-Modal CNN with Pseudo-Labeling and Rank Averaging
summary: Melanoma classification from dermoscopic images and patient metadata using EfficientNet/SE-ResNeXt backbones with domain-specific augmentations, metadata concatenation, pseudo-labeling on prior competition data, and rank-average ensembling across 15+ models.
dejargonized_summary: Detect skin cancer from photographs by training image-recognition networks with realistic data distortions, combining image features with patient information, adding pseudo-labeled historical data, and averaging rankings across many models.

inputs.name: dermoscopic_images
inputs.constraints: Shape (N, H, W, 3). RGB dermoscopic images at varying resolutions.

inputs.name: patient_metadata
inputs.constraints: Columns: age, sex, anatomical site of lesion.

planning_constraints.subject: augmentation_for_class_imbalance
planning_constraints.statement: Domain-specific augmentations (microscope artifacts, hair overlay) must be applied during training to improve robustness.
planning_constraints.rationale: Melanoma is extremely rare in the dataset (<2%); augmentations simulate real-world dermoscopic variation and help prevent overfitting to the majority class.

planning_constraints.subject: metadata_fusion
planning_constraints.statement: Patient metadata must be concatenated with CNN embeddings before the final classification head.
planning_constraints.rationale: Age, sex, and anatomical site provide strong priors for melanoma risk that complement visual features.

stages.name: Microscope Augmentation
stages.description: Apply domain-specific augmentations: circular black masks simulating dermoscope borders, fake hair overlay, and CutMix. Uses Albumentations and custom transforms.
stages.dejargonized_description: Add realistic distortions to training images like circular borders, fake hairs, and image mixing to help the model handle real-world dermoscopic variation.

inputs.name: dermoscopic_images
inputs.constraints: Shape (N, H, W, 3). Raw dermoscopic images.

outputs.name: augmented_images
outputs.constraints: Shape (N_aug, H, W, 3). Augmented dermoscopic images.

guarantees: Augmented images simulate realistic dermoscopic artifacts.
family_notes: Hair overlay and microscope border augmentations are specific to dermoscopy and significantly improve generalization.

stages.name: Image Backbone Training
stages.description: Train EfficientNet B3-B7 and SE-ResNeXt backbones on augmented dermoscopic images using Focal Loss to handle extreme class imbalance (<2% positive rate).
stages.dejargonized_description: Train several powerful image-recognition networks on the skin images, using a special loss function that pays extra attention to the rare cancer cases.

outputs.name: image_embeddings
outputs.constraints: Shape (N, D). Penultimate layer embeddings from CNN backbone.

guarantees: Embeddings capture visual features relevant to melanoma detection.
family_notes: Focal Loss down-weights easy negatives and up-weights hard examples, critical for <2% positive rate.

stages.name: Metadata Concatenation
stages.description: Extract the penultimate embedding layer from each CNN backbone and concatenate with encoded patient metadata (age, sex, anatomical location).
stages.dejargonized_description: Combine the image features extracted by the neural network with patient information like age, sex, and where the lesion is on the body.

outputs.name: fused_features
outputs.constraints: Shape (N, D + M). Concatenated image and metadata features.

preconditions: Image embeddings and metadata are available and aligned by sample.
guarantees: Output contains both visual and clinical information.

stages.name: Meta Head
stages.description: Pass the concatenated image embedding + metadata vector through a small MLP for final binary classification (melanoma vs. benign).
stages.dejargonized_description: Feed the combined image and patient features through a small neural network to produce the final cancer probability.
guarantees: Output is a calibrated probability per sample.

stages.name: Pseudo-Labeling
stages.description: Use trained models to predict on old 2018/2019 ISIC competition datasets, then add high-confidence pseudo-labeled samples to the training pool to increase effective dataset size.
stages.dejargonized_description: Apply trained models to older competition datasets to generate predicted labels, then add these extra labeled examples to the training data.

inputs.name: model_predictions
inputs.constraints: Predictions from trained models on external data.

outputs.name: pseudo_labeled_dataset
outputs.constraints: Extended training set with pseudo-labeled external images.

preconditions: Initial models are trained and external data is available.
guarantees: Pseudo-labeled samples expand the training pool with high-confidence examples.
family_notes: Pseudo-labeling leverages the large volume of unlabeled historical competition data to boost effective sample size.

stages.name: Rank Average Ensemble
stages.description: Rank-average predictions across 15+ CNN backbone variants and seeds. Each model's predictions are converted to ranks, averaged, then converted back to probabilities.
stages.dejargonized_description: Combine predictions from many different models by converting each to rankings, averaging the rankings, to get a final robust prediction.

inputs.name: model_predictions
inputs.constraints: List of (N,) prediction arrays from 15+ models.

preconditions: All individual model predictions are available.
guarantees: Rank averaging is robust to different prediction scales across models.
family_notes: Rank averaging is preferred over simple averaging because it is invariant to monotonic transformations of individual model outputs.

edges.provenance: Dermoscopic images with domain-specific augmentations applied.
Penultimate layer embeddings from CNN backbone.
Concatenated image embeddings and patient metadata.
Model predictions used to pseudo-label external datasets.
Per-model predictions collected for rank averaging.

audit.rationale: 1st place SIIM-ISIC Melanoma Classification solution. Multi-modal approach combining CNN image backbones with patient metadata, domain-specific augmentations, pseudo-labeling, and rank-average ensembling.
audit.dejargonized_summary: Detect skin cancer by training image networks with realistic dermoscopic distortions, combining image features with patient info, adding pseudo-labeled historical data, and averaging rankings across many models.
provenance_notes: Source: Kaggle SIIM-ISIC Melanoma Classification 1st place solution (2020)
uncertainty_notes: Pseudo-labeling on historical competition data assumes similar data distribution across years.
Focal Loss hyperparameters are tuned to the specific class imbalance ratio of this dataset.
